sources.title: Your Europe (EU): Roaming, using a mobile phone in the EU
Italian Electronic Communications Code, art. 98-undetricies: identifying users (Italian)

whatItIs: Optional. EU students can keep their home SIM at home prices, but on a long stay the operator may start charging extra. For a long stay, the EU suggests a local SIM.
With a SIM from outside the EU, roaming costs depend on your home operator.

bring.text: A passport or ID card; the shop keeps a copy. Non-EU citizens can use a passport or residence permit.
Your passport, if you have one, even as an EU citizen: some operators do not accept ID cards from other EU countries
Your tax code, if you already have it: the law does not require it, but operators often ask for it
An address in Italy, such as your rental contract or a signed letter from your host with a copy of their ID, if the operator asks

afterArrival: Buy the SIM in an operator's shop. Shops are usually more flexible than online activation if you have no tax code.
Compare offers yourself; this guide does not recommend an operator.
commonMistakes: Bringing only an EU ID card. At least one operator asked for a passport instead.
Counting on online activation. Without an Italian digital identity or tax code it may not work, so a shop is the safer choice.
whatComesNext: Nothing in this checklist is confirmed to need an Italian number. Some services, such as banks, may ask for one.
